title: Annealed multifractal exponents of the leaf-growth measure on uniform plane binary trees
author: Alessandra Caraceni; Nicolas Curien; Robin Stephenson
difficulty_reason: The prior uniform leaf-growth construction and Catalan estimates leave all real-power moments and their exponent unresolved, especially for negative powers at the singular endpoints. The authors derive the exact two-subtree moment recurrence and build upper/lower inductive comparison barriers controlled by the sign of an improper integral. The new uniform endpoint estimates, including separate bounds valid independently of the signs of the powers, justify the required dominated limit and identify the unique exponent throughout its stated parameter domain.

Uniform rooted plane binary trees with n internal vertices; the unique symmetric recursive leaf-growth measure uses the explicit C(a,b) of formula4. For every real alpha, the expected sum of leaf masses to power alpha+1 equals n^(-beta(alpha)+o(1)), where beta is the unique zero of integral2 and beta<2alpha+3/2. Full new proof26–28 read, including moment recursion, uniqueness and integrability of the exponent, dominated endpoint asymptotics and upper/lower induction. Necessary measure/tree definitions8–11 and Catalan estimates12–14 retained; Mn interpretation22 included. Explicit growth scheme Theorem2.4 is prior Caraceni–Stauffer2020 Proposition5.1, with authored recurrence and construction context retained. No quenched multifractal spectrum, conjectured maximal mass exponent, continuum scaling or ordinary d-ary extension selected.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors derive an exact moment recursion for the leaf-growth mass, identify its critical exponent through an improper integral, and prove matching power-law bounds by endpoint-dominated Riemann sums and inductive barriers. This probabilistic fractal asymptotic analysis exceeds ordinary qualifying examinations.
